pinterest.title: Macedonian Wedding Traditions in Order: From the Asking to the Last Oro
pinterest.description: Macedonian wedding traditions often run in an order many families still keep: the asking and the engagement, choosing the kum and kuma, the gifts, the wedding flag and the bread, collecting the bride, the Orthodox crowning, the welcome at the groom's home and the oro. Customs vary by village, region and family, so ask parents and grandparents which ones you will keep.

pinterest.title: What Is the Oro? The Macedonian Wedding Dance Explained
pinterest.description: The oro is a line or circle dance, with guests linked by the hands, and at a Macedonian wedding it can run for much of the night. Live musicians are part of many Macedonian weddings, and guests who have never danced it are usually pulled into the line within minutes: the steps are learned by following the person in front. Wear shoes you can dance in.

pinterest.title: Macedonian Orthodox Wedding: The Crowning, the Kum and the Kuma
pinterest.description: At a Macedonian Orthodox wedding, the couple wear wedding crowns during the service and the kum takes part alongside them. The kum and kuma are the couple's wedding sponsors, and many families treat the role as a lifelong bond. Your priest sets the order of service and can walk you through it, including which language it will be in.

slides: Macedonian wedding traditions you did not know, in the order many families still keep them
Before the wedding: the asking and the engagement. The groom's family calls on the bride's family to ask for her hand, often over food and drink.
The kum and kuma are the couple's wedding sponsors. Many families honour them most after the couple themselves, so seat them first.
The wedding flag and the bread. A decorated wedding banner, not a national flag, and a round wedding bread that families bake and decorate in their own way.
The wedding day: the groom's shave, collecting the bride with family and musicians, then the Orthodox crowning, where the couple wear wedding crowns.
Then the oro. A line or circle dance, guests linked by the hands, and it can run for much of the night.
Customs vary by village, region and family. Ask your parents and grandparents which ones you will keep.

instagram_carousel.caption:
Most lists of Macedonian wedding traditions stop at the party tricks. Our new guide follows a wedding in the order many families still keep it: the asking, the engagement, choosing the kum and kuma, the gifts, the flag and the bread, collecting the bride, the Orthodox crowning, the welcome and the oro.

A few things couples tell us they did not know:
The kum and kuma, the couple's wedding sponsors, are often the people families honour most after the couple themselves.
The wedding flag is a wedding banner, not a national flag, and families decorate it in their own way.
In the mountain village of Galičnik, one selected couple is still married each year in the traditional regional style at the Galičnik Wedding Festival.

Customs vary by village, region and family, and Macedonian-Australian families often adapt them. None of that makes a wedding less Macedonian.

Marrying in North Macedonia as an Australian? The guide also covers which Australian mission helps (the Embassy in Belgrade) and what to check before you book.

Which custom does your family keep? Tell us in the comments, or talk to a Wedded Advisor about your wedding. Full guide at the link in our bio.
